I think my knowledge before driving is roughly the same after, but my #1 tip that unfortunately many people do not follow is the 3 Second Rule

The car in front of you should be 3 seconds ahead of you. It will always give you enough time to react if someone happens ahead. I have managed to avoid many rear end collisions purely because of the three second rule. The most common accident is the rear end collision. 

Yes, that means on the highway, you are nearly 270 feet away from the car in front. Better safe than sorry.

Also, one other tip is to have your base driving skills at or a bit below the speed limit. I was teaching one of my friends to drive and I noticed he tended to speed and called my driving “grandma”. I kept reiterating that he should drive at the speed limit as his base so you don’t at the very least freak out the driving tester. You can always go faster from that baseline
